text.p: These are significant stories in the Nigerian press on Wednesday. Reuters has not verified these stories and does not vouch for their accuracy.
- University teachers will get pay rise soon, Nigeria's number two Lieutenant-General Oladipo Diya tells public lecture.

- Experts begin comprehensive inspection of maintenance records of planes belonging to ADC airline, whose jet crashed on November 7 killing all 142 on board, says director of safety regulations and monitoring in aviation ministry, Ibrahim Mamman.
- Forex demand by banks down by $6.29 million in weekly auction last week from the previous week.
- Nigerian stock exchange freezes share price of troubled ADC airline, whose plane crashed three weeks ago.
- Military ruler General Sani Abacha says in message to conference of air force officers that there will be no sacred cows in his anti-corruption war.
- Court starts hearing in multi-million naira suit over insurance account of state-owned Nigerian National Petroleum Corporation.
- Nigeria Airways DC 10 aircraft impounded in London over a two million sterling debt owed to British finance company Equator Leasing Finance.
- Opposition NADECO group petitions Commonwealth secretariat in London over recent visit of Commonwealth team to Nigeria; denounces team for not meeting anti-government groups.
- Helicopter makes forced landing on a road in southeastern oil city of Port Harcourt because of mechanical fault; no one was hurt and fault was rectified and chopper took off few hours later.
